ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a circle, with four points C, D, E, F marked on the circumference, where C is on the left, D is above, E is on the right, and F is below. Line segments DC and DF start from point D, forming an angle marked as 40°, namely ∠CDF. The figure also marks 98° near the upper-right arc, but what is sought is arc CF. Reasoning: ∠CDF is an inscribed angle, and the arc intercepted by its two sides DC and DF is arc CF. According to the inscribed angle theorem, the measure of the intercepted arc is equal to 2 times the measure of the inscribed angle. Therefore m arc CF = 2 × 40° = 80°.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram as a circle with points C, D, E, F on the circumference. The segment DC and the vertical segment DF meet at D, and the marked angle between them is 40°. Since angle CDF is an inscribed angle whose sides intercept arc CF, use the inscribed angle theorem: the intercepted arc has twice the measure of the inscribed angle. Therefore m arc CF = 2 × 40° = 80°.
